newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe government defends Malaysia power deal.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe government defends Malaysia power deal.

text.p: The Zimbabwean government on Friday defended a deal with Malaysia to privatise Zimbabwe's power utility, ZESA, following stinging criticism by ZESA authorities about the way the agreement was reached.

"Government has every right to decide how it wants investment to come into the country. If these gentlemen do not agree with what their principal has decided to do, they are quite free to resign," a senior Ministry of Transport and Energy official told state media.
Officials from the Zimbabwe Electricity Supply Authority (ZESA) opposing the deal with the Malaysians were unavailable for comment.

The independent Financial Gazette newspaper reported on Thursday that ZESA chairman Solomon Tawengwa was requesting the government to rescind a letter of intent it signed last week with Malaysian power producer YTL Corp Bhd.
According to the letter, YTL would invest Z$6 billion (U.S.$580 million) in the privatisation of ZESA's Hwange Power Station in northern Zimbabwe.

Tawengwa said the government had not informed ZESA of the deal which he said was contrary to the southern African country's efforts to economically empower the majority blacks and would result in increases in electricity tariffs.

He said it was a departure from an earlier government agreement to follow tender procedures. ZESA had already invited bids and six companies had been shortlisted, top of them a British company, while YTL was at the bottom of the list.
On Friday, the Energy Ministry official said: "It is all nonsense that government has sold out to the Malaysians. This is a business arrangement and it is investment."
